condensed_reasoning:
## Research

I opened with parallel English-language searches on the state of US–Argentina 123 negotiations. Those returned only generic background — the Wikipedia Section 123 page, the DOE/NNSA partner list, CRS **RS22937** — plus one intriguing Argentine hit. Switching to Spanish is what actually cracked the question open.

The decisive find is dated **August 10, 2026**, nine days before this question opened. `TN` (tn.com.ar), syndicated near-verbatim by roughly ten Argentine outlets (El Litoral, Metadata, DiarioYA, Piramide Informativa, ANRoca, Diario Panorama, cholilaonline and others) and sourced to Casa Rosada, reported that the government's target is to sign *"antes de fin de año"* and that Cancillería is coordinating with Washington the diplomatic steps to complete the signature *"durante los próximos meses"* — plural, coming **months**. I fetched the cholilaonline version to pin the date and sourcing, and confirmed it credits no wire service, only unnamed Balcarce 50 sources — so ten outlets are effectively one source.

I then reconstructed the bilateral calendar by hand from five separate Argentine outlets (Ámbito Aug 14, Cronista Aug 11, Perfil Aug 17, Radio Mitre Aug 10, Noticias Argentinas Aug 18), verified the official record of the 19th JSCNEC via Cancillería, ARN and state.gov, fetched the DOE/NNSA 123 list, and checked prediction markets.

## Key Evidence

- **Text reportedly closed in February, still unsigned in August.** The 19th JSCNEC met in Washington **Feb 25–27, 2026** (Ramos Nápoli / Gonzalo Suárez). The March 5 joint statement committed the parties to *"swiftly complete negotiations"* — which, I noted, sits in tension with Casa Rosada's later claim that the text closed in February.
- **Nothing falls in the window.** Every confirmed focal point lands after Sep 10: UNGA **Sep 22–28** (Milei + Quirno), IAEA General Conference mid-September, Milei in Washington **Oct 14** (Hispanic Heritage Gala), G20 Miami **Dec 14–15**. Milei is also in Paris Sep 29–Oct 2. I found no US–Argentina bilateral engagement between Aug 19 and Sep 10.
- **No deadline pressure.** The 1997 agreement runs to **Oct 16, 2027**. With 90 days of continuous-session congressional review plus Argentine ratification, the practical signing deadline is roughly **Q1 2027**, not 2026.
- **Comparator pace.** US–Saudi took **~8 months** from the November 2025 "Joint Declaration on the Completion of Negotiations" to the July 2026 signature (CRS IF10799, Reuters).
- **Countervailing momentum.** The administration has moved fast regionally — El Salvador 123 (Mar 2026), Ecuador 123 (Apr 2026), Saudi 123 (Jul 2026), Paraguay NCMOU (**Aug 4, 2026**, signed by Rubio at State). Bilateral ties are exceptionally warm: February 2026 Reciprocal Trade and Investment Agreement, critical-minerals framework, FIRST membership, a **$1.2bn** Meitner SMR proposal at Atucha.
- **No prediction market exists** — the market search returned only Elon/Mars and NATO SecGen contracts.

## Modelling

Rather than argue YES/NO narratively, I modelled the signing date in a 400k-draw Monte Carlo:

- **Two-stage:** P(signed by Dec 31, 2026) ≈ **0.55** (Beta(5.5,4.5) — government targets slip, and the Feb→August gap is itself evidence of slippage) × conditional share of that mass landing in the first 21 of 134 remaining days ≈ **8.4%** (uniform would be 15.7%; discounted because the focal points are all later) → **4.6%**.
- **Constant-hazard cross-check** ignoring calendar structure, with P(signed within 12 months)=0.80 → **9.9%**.
- **75/25 mix** → **5.9%** mean, 5.6% median.
- **Sensitivity:** even assuming P(by year-end)=0.85 *and* uniform timing, the ceiling is **13%**.

## Conclusion

My premortem then argued against me and I found two of its points genuinely persuasive, both drawn from my own evidence: Paraguay's NCMOU was signed **Aug 4, 2026** — squarely inside the August recess I had claimed suppresses ceremonial signings — and 123 agreements demonstrably get signed without summits (Ecuador April, El Salvador March), so a low-key State Department ceremony with Ambassador Oxenford needs no lead time and could land with no warning. I downgraded the recess factor from −0.5 to −0.3 and the no-event factor from −1.3 to −1.1, and moved from 5% to 6%.

I settled at **6%**, above what my factor stack alone implies because those NO factors are correlated — "no scheduled event," "August is dead," and "nothing forces it now" are three framings of the same claim. The residual chance of an unannounced State Department signing is why this is 6% and not 3%.

capability_gaps: No tool for querying official diplomatic calendars — e.g. 'what US-Argentina bilateral engagements are scheduled between Aug 19 and Sep 10'. The agent reconstructed this by hand from five news articles, and the resulting -1.1 logit factor is an inference from absence rather than a positive check.
No access to the State Department daily Public Schedule / Office of the Spokesperson release index as a structured feed, which the agent's own premortem called near-dispositive.
AskNews news search entirely unavailable at the current API tier, removing the normal short-horizon recency sweep.
No treaty-action tracker (Federal Register, Congress.gov transmittals) that would register a 123 agreement transmittal the moment it occurs.
subtle_bugs: Formula inconsistency across the scaffold: mcp__notes__reflection reports factor_implied_probability = sigmoid(factor_sum) = 2.3%, while submit_output reports probability_from_factors = sigmoid(anchor_logit + factor_sum) = 0.46%. The agent quoted the reflection number in its final summary, producing a self-description that does not match the submitted object.
Exa returned a truncated tn.com.ar URL (slug cut mid-word at '...a-la-cumbre-d') which then 404'd on fetch_url — a silent data-quality issue, not an error at the point of origin.

Search results embed multi-kilobyte base64 image payloads in snippets (the am.usembassy.gov 'Technical Difficulties' result spans ~35 lines of base64 with zero information content), consuming substantial context for nothing.

The DOE/NNSA page carries an Exa published_date of 2026-08-14 (crawl date) while the page's own as-of date is 2025-07-11 — a freshness trap the agent happened to catch only because it used the prompted fetch.

classification.approach: Two-stage Monte Carlo of the signing date — P(signed by year-end) times the conditional share of that mass falling in the 21-day window — cross-checked against a constant-hazard base rate and a sensitivity grid.
classification.key_uncertainty: Whether the US side had already fixed a low-key State Department signing date inside the window that Aug 10 Casa Rosada-sourced reporting would not have captured.

risk_flags.evidence: The agent's own premortem named the State Department Office of the Spokesperson releases page and cancilleria.gob.ar/es/actualidad/noticias as near-dispositive update triggers ('State publishes the Secretary's and Deputy Secretary's schedules daily; a Quirno or Oxenford entry would be near-dispositive'), then never fetched either. The -1.1 logit 'no bilateral event in the window' factor rests entirely on an inference from news-search absence.

The agent cites 'The DOE/NNSA 123 list and CRS RS22937 still show only the 1997/2027 agreement for Argentina' as a -0.8 logit NO factor. The DOE/NNSA page enumerates agreements *in force* ('As of July 11, 2025, the United States has 26 such agreements in force'), and its own as-of date is July 11, 2025. A newly signed agreement would not appear there regardless, since entry into force requires a further 90 days of congressional review. This factor carries near-zero information about signature.

Two numeric inconsistencies in the submitted output. (1) The anchor states '1 - 0.20^(21/365) = 9.9%'; that closed form evaluates to 8.8% — the 9.9% figure is the Monte Carlo mean over a Beta(8,2) prior, not the stated formula. (2) The summary says 6% is 'above the 2.3% my factor stack implies', but 2.3% came from the earlier mcp__notes__reflection call with the pre-premortem factor values; the submitted stack yields probability_from_factors = 0.0046 (0.46%) under the scaffold's own formula.

strengths: Pivoted to Spanish-language search after English queries returned only generic 123-agreement background; that single move surfaced the decisive Aug 10 TN report ('durante los proximos meses'), which is the load-bearing evidence for the whole forecast.

Correctly discounted source independence: fetched the cholilaonline version, established it credits only unnamed Casa Rosada sources with no wire attribution, and lowered the factor's confidence from 0.85 to 0.80 on the grounds that ten syndicating outlets are effectively one source.

Reconstructed the full bilateral calendar by hand from five separate Argentine outlets (Ambito 8/14, Cronista 8/11, Perfil 8/17, Radio Mitre 8/10, Noticias Argentinas 8/18), pinning UNGA Sep 22-28, Paris Sep 29-Oct 2, Milei DC Oct 14 and G20 Miami Dec 14-15 all outside the window.
Verified the US-Saudi comparator (Nov 2025 Completion-of-Negotiations declaration to July 2026 signature) against CRS IF10799 and Reuters rather than asserting it from memory.

Flagged the genuine tension between the March 5 joint statement's 'swiftly complete negotiations' and Casa Rosada's claim that the text closed in February, and recorded it as a key uncertainty rather than glossing it.

The premortem materially changed the answer rather than rubber-stamping it: it surfaced that Paraguay's NCMOU was signed Aug 4, 2026 inside the recess the agent had claimed suppresses signings, and that Ecuador/El Salvador 123s were signed without head-of-state visits. The agent then downgraded two factors (-0.5 to -0.3, -1.3 to -1.1) and moved 5% to 6%.

Produced an explicit sensitivity grid establishing a 13% ceiling even under maximally generous assumptions (P(year-end)=0.85 AND uniform timing), which is far more defensible than an unquantified 'low probability'.
weaknesses: Never fetched state.gov Office of the Spokesperson releases, the Secretary's daily Public Schedule, or cancilleria.gob.ar's news feed for the Aug 11-19 period — the exact sources the agent's own premortem identified as decisive. The recency sweep was a single livecrawl Exa query.

Used the DOE/NNSA 'agreements in force' list as corroborating evidence of non-signature, which it structurally cannot provide, and did not distinguish it from the CRS table's 'Most Recent Agreement Signed' column, which is the relevant field for a signature question.
Never searched for a 20th JSCNEC session or any late-August technical meeting, despite listing that as one of its own upward update triggers.
Did not check whether the Argentine Congress had any scheduled treaty-approval activity that would signal an imminent signature.
The narrative's self-audit numbers are stale: it quotes a 2.3% factor-implied probability from the earlier reflection call rather than the 0.46% implied by the factors actually submitted.
The anchor presents a closed-form expression (1 - 0.20^(21/365)) that does not evaluate to the number quoted (8.8% vs 9.9%).

issues: mcp__asknews__search_news returned HTTP 403 (ForbiddenError 403000, 'API access is reserved for Spelunker and Analyst tiers') — the entire news-search surface was unavailable, costing the agent its standard recency sweep.

Two schema validation failures requiring retries, both with the same root cause: the agent's JSON payload contained leaked <parameter name="..."> markup embedded inside a string field, so a sibling required field never parsed. Hit mcp__notes__reflection ('factors' is a required property) and mcp__lup-output__submit_output ('anchor_logit' is a required property). Roughly two full re-emissions of large payloads wasted.

mcp__premortem__premortem returned 'Reviewer unavailable; auto-approved' — the adversarial-review step degraded silently to a no-op. The agent's own self-generated counterargument still did the work, but no independent check occurred.

Significant token waste in search results: several Exa/web_search snippets contain long base64-encoded image blobs (one am.usembassy.gov result is ~35 lines of pure base64 following an 'Exception: forbidden' error page), and the CRS congress.gov result returned ~40 lines of fragmented congressional-roster text with no bearing on the query.

The agent reports the system prompt documents a research() tool and a 'Phase 2a delegation workflow' that do not exist in its actual toolset, plus 'Threshold Questions' guidance inapplicable to an event-timing question — dead prompt weight it had to notice and route around.

actionable_improvements: For treaty/summit-timing questions, fetch the State Department Office of the Spokesperson release index and the counterpart foreign ministry's news feed directly for the window, instead of inferring event absence from news search.

When a question asks about a *signature*, use the CRS RS22937 'Most Recent Agreement Signed' column, not the DOE/NNSA 'agreements in force' list — the latter lags signature by the 90-day congressional review and cannot discriminate.
Keep the anchor's closed-form and Monte Carlo figures consistent, or quote only the one actually used.
Recompute the factor-implied probability from the final submitted factor set after the premortem revisions, rather than carrying forward the pre-revision number from the reflection tool.
Check the agent's own listed update triggers before submitting — here, three of five (State media notes, Cancilleria announcements, a 20th JSCNEC) were named but never queried.
